goal: Join a machine-recovered Book proposal to the existing canonical Book parent only after explicit current-subject author ratification, using the qualified author-decision applicability guard, existing content-admission/version authority and existing lifecycle rebind authority. Do not create another workflow engine or lifecycle state machine.
integration_law: EBR-SC1 remains proposal/evidence state and never mutates canonical Book state directly.
Imported source identities are provenance/evidence, not Author Decision Queue governed-subject identities.
Recovery ratification is anchored to the current governed BookProject identity and current canonical manuscript identity; imported source refs remain evidence refs.
A recovered manuscript can be admitted only when the candidate revision graph has one selected candidate and no unresolved BLOCKING recovery finding remains.
The selected candidate's content digest is admitted as a new immutable MANUSCRIPT_MANIFEST version in the existing manuscript family; no historical edition/version is overwritten.
Every author-gated admission operation must pass BOOK-SYSTEM-CONTENT-ADMISSION-AUTHOR-DECISION-APPLICABILITY-GUARD-004.

After successful content admission, lifecycle history is rebound to the authorized parent successor through BOOK-SYSTEM-LIFECYCLE-CURRENT-PARENT-REBIND-001 with authority_kind CANONICAL_STATE_MUTATION.
Recovery admission does not change Book lifecycle status. Any lifecycle advance is a separate existing lifecycle-transition request subject to the canonical transition contract and evidence gates.
SYSTEM-ORCHESTRATOR remains durable execution authority; this adapter performs one bounded transactional composition only.

ratification_subject.primary: BOOK_PROJECT current state identity: object_id=book_project_id, object_version=STATE-<parent_state_version>, object_digest=digest(book_project)
ratification_subject.secondary: current canonical MANUSCRIPT_MANIFEST exact object/version/digest identity
ratification_subject.source_evidence: all RecoveredBookBaseline source_manifest source_ref values plus recovery baseline id/digest

required_input: current Author Decision Queue ledger containing an approved recovery-ratification resolution receipt
author decision id and resolution receipt id
output: post-admission parent state and version ledger
lifecycle rebind receipt and post-rebind lifecycle ledger
recovery admission receipt binding baseline digest, selected candidate, author decision/receipt, pre/post parent and lifecycle identities
resume directive that names the existing lifecycle exact-next boundary without performing an unauthorized lifecycle transition
fail_closed: baseline book_project_id conflicts with current BookProject when supplied
revision graph has no single selected candidate
any recovery finding severity is BLOCKING
selected candidate or source provenance is missing
author decision/queue receipt does not bind the exact current BookProject/manuscript ratification subject
author decision receipt is stale, mismatched or absent
selected recovered content is already an ambiguous/conflicting family successor
content admission fails any existing predecessor/currentness/provenance invariant
lifecycle ledger is not bound to the exact pre-admission parent
any attempted recovery admission changes lifecycle status
qualification_cases: clean recovered baseline plus exact current-subject ratification admits one immutable manuscript successor and rebinds lifecycle history
unresolved version ambiguity blocks before author/canonical mutation
ratification receipt for a different governed subject blocks
stale ratification after current manuscript changes blocks
same admitted content cannot overwrite historical predecessor lineage
successful recovery admission preserves lifecycle project status and lifecycle history
NEW_EDITION recovery preserves prior-edition lineage in the recovery receipt and does not rewrite the prior edition
recovery engine output remains unchanged/no direct canonical mutation

automatic lifecycle stage advancement/resume placement beyond an exact-next directive
